newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba -- Bonn contribution to IMF quotas seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Buba -- Bonn contribution to IMF quotas seen higher.

text.p: The current review of the level of the amount of funds countries pay to finance the International Monetary Fund must include a reweighting of the burden of contributions, the Bundesbank said on Wednesday.
Bonn's contribution to the fund could be expected to increase in such a review, the bank said in its annual report.
The IMF's quota subscriptions, or membership fees, form a common pool of resources which member countries may draw on in times of need.
The review of the IMF's quotas would have to take into account the increased level of world trade and the increased financing needs its member countries had as a result of this, the Bundesbank said.

It declined to comment on the likely size of increase in the overall quotas which might be determined in the current review of the institution's funding level, but said it expected Germany to bear a larger part of the total burden.
"Independently of the volume of a quota increase there is a need to correct the distribution of the quotas," it said.

"The quota structure should reflect the relative importance of the individual countries in the world economy," the report said. "Germany is among the countries which need considerable adjustment on the upside."
